Verified.Point: FulfillmentRecord model carries only: orderReference (PK), printifyOrderId?, blueprintId, printProviderIdSelected?, routingOption, productTitle, variantReference, decorationMethod, fulfillmentStatus, recordedAt, updatedAt. No name, age, audience, email, address, or conversation id exists as a column. The boundary is structural at the persistence layer — prohibited fields are impossible to write because they do not exist, not merely omitted by convention.

Write path (fulfillment-record.server.js) builds an explicit telemetry allowlist and passes only that to Prisma. The full printifyOrder object is received, but only line_items[].print_provider_id / .status / .variant_id / .external_id and order .id / .status are read from it — the address_to / recipient block is never touched. Two independent structural guards, not one.

Idempotency is a real upsert keyed on the orderReference primary key. Re-delivery updates in place; no duplicate row. An incomplete re-delivery preserves the previously resolved provider and status (guarded update spreads).

printProviderIdSelected is nullable and resolved from the concrete provider on the order response, never the literal 99. routingOption holds 99. Matches the directive's "record the WHAT, resolve the concrete provider later" design.

Migration 20260913010000_add_fulfillment_record is CREATE TABLE + three indexes only; the seven existing models are untouched. A paired rollback.sql drops indexes then table in correct order. migration_lock.toml provider = sqlite (no provider mismatch).

printify.server.js takes the token from process.env only, never hardcodes it, and its error messages surface Printify's status/message without echoing the token. Test 4 asserts this: a 422 failure throws the Printify message, does NOT contain the token, and writes no record.

The recorder is wired into the Printify submission seam (printify.server.js submitOrder / refreshOrder). No deployed route, Shopify webhook, or live order event triggers it yet. This is the correct unwired-but-tested state — it is exactly what keeps the claim at Tested and out of Production.

I re-ran the suite myself (stubbing only the @prisma/client import so db.server.js loads; the fulfillment tests inject their own in-memory database and never touch real Prisma). Fulfillment: 4/4 pass on real logic, including the identity-rejection test (fixture deliberately carries address_to first_name/last_name/email/address1 and the test asserts none persists) and the token-non-leak test. Full suite: 42/42 pass, 0 fail.

OpenItemsAndFindings.Finding: Confirm the exact JSON path of the resolved print provider in a genuine Printify Choice (option 99) order response before depending on the enrichment. Ties to OI-15 (the physical VT-6 sample) and the "prepared, unwired" Printify status. Code degrades safely if the field is absent, so this does not block the Tested rung.

Codex honestly recorded: replaying the entire migration chain into a completely empty SQLite path throws Prisma's generic schema-engine error; the deployment-representative upgrade from the current DB passes cleanly. Operational meaning: normal Railway deploy (new migration on top of the existing /data/dev.db) is unaffected; a from-scratch rebuild — new volume, disaster recovery, migrate reset, CI-from-empty — would fail. Most plausible location (INFERENCE, not reproduced — engine binaries blocked this session): the prior 20260912180000_bind_pkce_state_to_request migration, which uses the PRAGMA foreign_keys OFF / redefine-table pattern. Component 1's own migration is verified clean additive and is NOT the cause. Closes when a from-empty replay is made to pass, or the operator accepts the DR limitation in writing.

.gitattributes applies `text eol=lf` to `_lazycustoms/ops/evidence/live_runs/**` — a glob that catches the binary PNG evidence fixtures. Git is EOL-normalizing binaries and stripping CR bytes (e.g. 1,651,937 → 1,651,910 bytes), which changes the very bytes the comment says it wants to "hash exact." Recommended fix (owner's edit, not applied here): mark the PNGs binary, e.g. `_lazycustoms/ops/evidence/live_runs/**/*.png binary`.
